findings.highlight: had this been right before a concert or a competition
findings.evidenceJa: これがコンサートやコンクールの直前だと
findings.explanation: Kazusa describes her habitual schedule whenever a concert or competition is imminent: she plays during every waking, non-eating hour. The translation turns it into an unreal past counterfactual.
findings.japanese:
「で、これがコンサートやコンクールの直前だと、
寝て食べる以外の時間は全部弾いてる」
findings.todokanai: "Well, had this been right before a concert or a competition, I'd be practicing every second I'm not eating or sleeping."

findings.highlight: "It sure is. That's why it's only natural that I don't know anything about doing chores or having a private life. I simply don't have the time."
findings.evidenceJa:
「そうだよ。だから家事とか私生活のことなんか
何もできなくて当然なんだ。
する暇がないからな」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she cannot handle household and private-life matters, while Todokanai TL says she knows nothing about chores or having a private life.
findings.japanese:
「そうだよ。だから家事とか私生活のことなんか
何もできなくて当然なんだ。
する暇がないからな」
findings.todokanai: "It sure is. That's why it's only natural that I don't know anything about doing chores or having a private life. I simply don't have the time."

findings.highlight: when you weren't a professional pianist
findings.evidenceJa: ピアノやってなかった頃だって
findings.explanation: Haruki refers to the period when Kazusa was not playing piano, not a period when she played but lacked professional status. The translation invents a career-stage distinction.
findings.japanese:
「お前は単に物臭なだけだろ。
ピアノやってなかった頃だって全然…」
findings.todokanai: "No, that's just because you're lazy. Even when you weren't a professional pianist, you weren't at all…"

findings.highlight: making me feel even more uncertain
findings.evidenceJa: 余計にヤバい気持ちになってしまう
findings.explanation: Seeing Kazusa's hidden side makes Haruki's feelings more dangerous or alarming to him, feeding the vicious cycle. 'Uncertain' reduces an explicit sense of emotional peril to indecision.
findings.japanese:
…そのせいで、
かずさが普段見せない一面を引き出してしまい、
余計にヤバい気持ちになってしまう。
findings.todokanai: …Thanks to that, Kazusa shows a side of herself she usually keeps hidden, making me feel even more uncertain.

findings.highlight: an advertisement belonging to a familiar magazine
findings.evidenceJa: お馴染みの写真週刊誌の中吊り広告
findings.explanation: Haruki sees the hanging train advertisement for a familiar photo weekly. The translation loses both the photo-weekly format and the fact that the ad is suspended inside the train, weakening the spatial reveal that makes Kazusa immediately recognizable.
findings.japanese:
かずさに説教を垂れつつふと見上げた先の、
お馴染みの写真週刊誌の中吊り広告。
findings.todokanai: As I was lecturing Kazusa, I happened to look up to see an advertisement belonging to a familiar magazine.

findings.highlight: Homecoming of the second generation genius pianist Touma Kazusa
findings.evidenceJa: 初来日・天才二世ピアニスト冬馬かずさ
findings.explanation: The sensational headline calls this Kazusa's first visit to Japan. The translation instead calls it a homecoming, reversing the tabloid's stated arrival status.
findings.japanese:
『初来日・天才二世ピアニスト冬馬かずさ
母親譲りの唯我独尊』
findings.todokanai: "Homecoming of the second generation genius pianist Touma Kazusa. Inherited self-centeredness from mother."

findings.highlight: I don't want to show you to anyone
findings.evidenceJa: 『見せたくない』気持ちの方が強かった
findings.explanation: Haruki admits that his stronger feeling is not wanting to show the hurtful advertisement to Kazusa. The translation instead says he does not want to show Kazusa to other people, making both contrasted motives about concealing her identity and erasing his protective concern for what she reads.
findings.japanese:
本当は『気づかれたくない』より
『見せたくない』気持ちの方が強かったけど、
いちいちそんな心情を説明する必要なんかない。
findings.todokanai: In truth, rather than "I don't want anyone to recognize you," my feelings lean closer to "I don't want to show you to anyone." But there's no reason to explain every single sentiment like that to her.

findings.highlight: a cushion for Kazusa while she's in Japan
findings.evidenceJa: かずさと日本との間の、緩衝材
findings.explanation: Haruki casts himself as a buffer between Kazusa and Japan, mediating their harmful contact. The translation makes him a generic cushion for her during her stay and removes the two-sided relationship.
findings.japanese:
ただ、俺がこうしないと。
かずさと日本との間の、緩衝材にならないと…
findings.todokanai: All that matters is that I become a cushion for Kazusa while she's in Japan.

findings.highlight: she's beginning to allow herself to touch my body
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の体が触れるのを許し始めた
findings.explanation: Haruki interprets Kazusa's relaxation as beginning to allow his body to touch hers. The translation makes Kazusa the person actively allowing herself to touch Haruki, reversing agency inside an already focalized consent reading.
findings.japanese:
だって、全身の緊張が解けたから。
少しだけ、俺の体が触れるのを許し始めたから。
findings.todokanai: I can tell because her whole body doesn't feel tense anymore. And she's beginning to allow herself to touch my body, even if only a little.

findings.highlight: I'm not sure if my judgement was correct
findings.evidenceJa: その事実に俺の判断が効いたのかどうかは正直よくわからなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki is unsure whether his intervention actually contributed to the passengers failing to recognize Kazusa. The translation instead questions whether his judgment was correct, changing causal efficacy into moral or practical correctness.
findings.japanese:
その事実に俺の判断が効いたのかどうかは
正直よくわからなかったけど、
でも、今後もこういう判断が発生することだけは実感した。
findings.todokanai: Facing that fact, I'm not sure if my judgement was correct, but I do realize now that I'll have to make this kind of judgement many times in the future.

findings.evidenceJa: アクセサリショップだった
findings.explanation: Their first stop is an accessory shop, where they buy a comb ornament and disguise items. The translation relocates the scene to a beauty salon.
findings.japanese:
電車から降りて俺たちが最初に目指したのは、
家電量販店でも家具店でもなく、
アクセサリショップだった。
findings.todokanai: Our first destination after we got off the train was not an electronic store or a furniture store, but rather a beauty salon.

findings.highlight: the beautiful spectacled young lady next door
findings.evidenceJa: その辺にいる眼鏡の綺麗なお姉さん
findings.explanation: The phrase means an ordinary beautiful woman with glasses one might see around town. 'Next door' is not present and is especially misleading here because Kazusa has literally just moved into the apartment beside Haruki.
findings.japanese:
これで『ただ今話題沸騰のピアニスト冬馬かずさ』改め、
『その辺にいる眼鏡の綺麗なお姉さん』の出来上がり。
findings.todokanai: With this, she's no longer "the talk of the town pianist Touma Kazusa," but rather "the beautiful spectacled young lady next door."

findings.explanation: Haruki turns to the clerk and solicits agreement that the disguise suits Kazusa. The translation makes him provide an affirmative answer himself, reversing question and confirmation.

findings.evidenceJa: 後でまとめて精算するから
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will settle up or reimburse the purchases together later. The translation says only that she will calculate a total, omitting the payment that prompts Haruki's refusal.
findings.japanese:
「後でまとめて精算するから、
とりあえず渡しておいて…」
findings.todokanai: "I'll calculate the total later, so give it to me for now…"

findings.highlight: from telephone providers to furniture stores
findings.evidenceJa: 家電売り場と家具売り場を縦横無尽に走り回り
findings.explanation: They race through home-appliance and furniture departments to buy a refrigerator, table, and bed. The translation substitutes telephone service providers for the appliance section.
findings.japanese:
冷蔵庫、テーブル、ベッド、その他諸々。
家電売り場と家具売り場を縦横無尽に走り回り、
たった数時間で１０万以上も散財してしまった。
findings.todokanai: A fridge, a table, a bed etc. We went through everywhere from telephone providers to furniture stores, spending over 100000 yen in just a few hours.

findings.highlight: three months worth of fees for just a single month at their hotel, including deposits and key money
findings.evidenceJa: 敷金礼金合わせて三か月分を払う
findings.explanation: The Toumas pay three months' rent-equivalent in apartment deposit and key money for a roughly one-month stay. The translation moves these apartment-specific charges to a hotel and describes the stay itself as a month of hotel fees.
findings.japanese:
…なにしろたった一月程度の滞在のために、
敷金礼金合わせて三か月分を払う気前のいい一家だ。
findings.todokanai: …After all, this generous family has paid three months worth of fees for just a single month at their hotel, including deposits and key money.

findings.highlight: is the reason I came back to Japan
findings.evidenceJa: お前に最高の冬馬かずさを見せるためだけに、あたしは日本まで来た
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she came all the way to Japan only to show Haruki the very best Touma Kazusa. The translation preserves the motive but omits the exclusive 'only,' weakening the climactic declaration of singular purpose.
findings.japanese:
「だってさ…
お前に最高の冬馬かずさを見せるためだけに、
あたしは日本まで来たんだぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "After all… Showing you the absolute best of Touma Kazusa is the reason I came back to Japan."
